title: TF module pinbook and rollback checklist for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic compatibility & pinning playbook for Terraform modules and providers used by Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. Deliverables: a compatibility matrix (+tested permutations), recommended version constraints, CI gating for upgrades, automated health checks, and an actionable rollback checklist for staged rollouts.
compatibility_matrix: format: Provider | Module | Tested_min | Tested_max | Recommended_pin | Notes

hashicorp/aws | redwood/vpc | 4.58.0 | 5.8.0 | ~> 5.8, patch pins for modules | AWS provider 5.x required for new subnet defaults; pin modules to avoid drift when AWS provider 6.x drops deprecated args
hashicorp/azurerm | redwood/vnet | 3.47.0 | 3.81.0 | ~> 3.80 | Lock to minor until we validate upstream changes to azurerm_subnet delegation behavior
hashicorp/google | redwood/gke | 4.19.0 | 4.41.0 | >= 4.35, < 5.0 | Google provider 5.x changes IAM binding behavior; avoid until tested
hashicorp/kubernetes | redwood/k8s-bootstrap | 2.11.0 | 2.16.0 | ~> 2.16 | kube client auth changes in 2.17 impacted deploy timeouts in stage
terraform | redwood/modules | 1.5.6 | 1.6.7 | CLI constraint: >=1.5, <2.0; module pins: exact patch pins in release branches | Ensure CI uses consistent Terraform version matrix
random/provider | redwood/random-secrets | 3.1.0 | 3.2.1 | ~> 3.2 | No breaking changes observed; still pin to avoid surprises
pinning_policy: Major policy: Never automatically upgrade major provider versions. Treat major bumps as manual projects with a testing plan.
Minor policy: Allow minor upgrades behind canary pipelines if compatibility tests pass; prefer '~>' constraints to pick safe patch updates.
Module policy: Modules consumed by production Private stacks must be pinned to exact module commit/tag in the release branch (e.g., vpc@2025-11-branch or vpc@v1.2.3).
CLI policy: CI pipelines pin the terraform binary with tfenv; test against the full Terraform version matrix from the compatibility_matrix before merging provider bumps.
Dependency policy: When bumping a provider, update corresponding module tags in the same PR and run the full integration matrix in CI (see upgrade_playbook).
upgrade_playbook: 1) Create a dedicated branch: infra/tf-upgrade/<provider>-<target-version> with CHANGELOG and matrix summary.
2) Update provider constraints in module root and update module tags for consumers in same PR where possible.
3) Run local preflight: terraform init -upgrade -backend-config=... && terraform plan -var-file=ci.tfvars against a disposable test environment.
4) CI matrix: for each (Terraform version x Provider version) run: terraform init -> plan -> apply (on throwaway test account) -> smoke tests (see health_checks).
5) Canary rollout: deploy to 'canary' customer(s) or internal staging VPC pool for 48 hours; monitor logs and metrics.
6) Gradual rollout: schedule batched rollouts to 10% / 25% / 50% production pools with 24-72h observation windows and automated auto-rollback trigger on failure thresholds.
7) Post-upgrade: tag release, update module registry notes, and create ops runbook for new behaviors discovered.
Commands samples: 'terraform init -backend-config=... -upgrade', 'tfenv install 1.5.6 && tfenv use 1.5.6', 'make smoke-test-stack'
health_checks: Plan-level checks: use 'terraform plan -detailed-exitcode' and fail on any diffs to already applied infra unless the PR explicitly includes the expected changes.
State validation: run 'terraform state list' and diff resource counts against a known-good baseline; alert on unexpected replacements.
Runtime checks: post-apply smoke tests — create a test pod in each cluster, perform HTTP healthcheck against control-plane endpoints, validate DNS entries and route tables.
Service-level metrics: monitor request latency (p50/p95), error rates, and 'node provisioning' durations in Prometheus for 72h after upgrade.
Drift detection: scheduled weekly terraform plan runs (readonly) with automated PRs for detected drift; mark any provider-related drift as high priority.
Security checks: run static security scan on plan with 'tfsec' and run policy checks via Sentinel/Open Policy Agent in CI before merges.
rollback_plan: Preconditions: keep previous module tags and provider constraints available in a rollback branch; keep state snapshot backup (terraform state pull -> store in S3 with epoch timestamp).
Immediate rollback: if automated monitors breach thresholds in canary, trigger the rollback pipeline which checks out the rollback branch and runs 'terraform apply' to restore previous state.
Fallback steps: if terraform apply fails, follow emergency manual steps: 1) restore state from S3 snapshot; 2) run targeted resource replacements for broken resources; 3) escalate to oncall infra.
Communication: automatically open an incident channel, notify affected customers via status page with initial impact assessment and expected rollback ETA.
Postmortem: capture root cause, update the compatibility_matrix and pinning_policy, and schedule any additional tests required before next attempt.
automation_tasks: GH Actions: extend infra-ci to run the full (tf_version x provider_version) matrix — see github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/243 (WIP).
Registry sync: publish pinned module bundles to our private terraform registry and tag releases with tested matrix metadata.
State snapshot automation: implement nightly 'state-pull' job that archives state with TTL-backed retention and verifies checksums.
Upgrade job: create a scheduled job that proposes minor provider patch bumps as draft PRs with plan artifacts attached for review.
Runbook generator: auto-generate canary/rollback runbooks per PR with links to plan output, state snapshots, and monitored dashboards.
